chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what comes out from the nostrils of the animal and hits me. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (it is pure/permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is the nasal discharge of animals considered ritually pure or impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of minor impurities by ruling that animal nasal discharge is pure (*tahira*), thereby not requiring removal for valid prayer. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that unless a substance is explicitly defined as impure (*najis*) by textual evidence, its default state is purity, distinguishing it from other bodily excretions like urine or droppings.
